newsitem.title: FRANCE: Legras says EU wheat subsidies "not aggressive".
newsitem.headline: Legras says EU wheat subsidies "not aggressive".

text.p: Guy Legras, the European Commission's director general for agriculture, said on Wednesday the European Union was "not aggressive" when exporting its wheat with subsidies.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, Legras said export subsidies were currently needed to bridge the gap between European wheat and world prices.
"Subsidies are destined to bring European prices in line with world prices and allow normal exports without any intention to cut prices or to be aggressive," he said
Legras was reacting to recent criticism of EU subsidies by U.S. officials.
On Tuesday U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said he was prepared to use the Export Enhancement Program in response to EU subsidies if necessary.
Glickman also said he had written to EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler to express deep disappointment with his decision to resume grain export subsidies.

Legras said the European Union, which restored last week subsidies on its wheat exports after suspending them for more than a year, had no intention to engage in a confrontation with the United States.
"The Americans are perfectly aware that there is a gap between the dollar price of EU wheat and Chicago prices," he said.
Legras said that faced with prospects of a promising crop, the EU had to export its wheat and the United States was "aware of it".
But the Commission would in any case have a cautious export policy.
"We will remain cautious. Last week we sold at a high price ... $173-174 per tonne fob. That was above Chicago," he said.
On September 19 the European Union sold 237,470 tonnes of wheat at a maximum refund of 4.97 Ecus per tonne, worth some $173-174 per tonne on world markets.
Legras also said the Commission was not planning any special measures to encourage the export of EU wheat to targeted destinations.
